external-attack-surface.title: External attack surface management
external-attack-surface.intro: An acquisition brings in a customer portal that never made it into the parent company’s inventory. EASM helps the security team find the portal from the internet, establish whose it is, and check that the exposure is gone after the owner fixes it.
external-attack-surface.discoveryQuestion: Walk me through the last internet-facing asset your team learned about from someone else. How did you prove it was yours, find the owner and confirm the fix?

groups.question: Can we explain why a newly found asset belongs to us, a subsidiary, or a supplier?

offerings.description: Uses its own internet observations to identify exposed hosts and services and alert on changes. Its M&A guide describes attribution to business units.
offerings.question: Can an asset owner confirm the evidence linking a newly acquired subsidiary’s infrastructure?

offerings.description: Maps relationships between external assets and organizations, then prioritizes exposures using active validation.
offerings.question: Can the team explain why a previously unknown asset belongs to a particular business unit?

offerings.description: Maps external assets and infrastructure dependencies, provides discovery evidence, and adds reachability and threat context.
offerings.question: Can we distinguish assets we control from dependencies a supplier must fix?

offerings.description: Discovers unmanaged domains, IP addresses and cloud infrastructure, monitors changes and scores external exposures.
offerings.question: Which new discoveries were absent from our existing vulnerability inventory?

offerings.description: Combines agentless discovery, daily inventory updates and grouped findings that can be tracked through remediation.
offerings.question: How many previously untracked assets can we assign to a responsible team?

groups.question: Which new assets does the module surface in the workflow our team already uses?

offerings.question: Can the SOC take a previously unknown service from discovery to an assigned response?

offerings.question: Which external assets were missing from the coverage our VM team already manages?

offerings.description: Discovers internet-facing infrastructure within CSAM and alerts on new assets, changes and critical issues.
offerings.question: Can we reconcile a newly attributed public asset with our Qualys inventory?

offerings.question: Can a discovery be matched to an existing internal record or routed for ownership review?

offerings.question: What external coverage is included in our Falcon quote, and who can act on a finding?

offerings.question: For a newly disclosed issue, what asset-specific evidence would a remediation owner receive?

offerings.question: Which findings are validated by Atlas, and when would we need Nova?

offerings.description: Tests internet-facing assets and web applications to validate which externally reachable security weaknesses matter.
offerings.question: What evidence distinguishes an exposed service from a confirmed security impact?

groups.question: Can a threat report be tied to an asset we own or a supplier we depend on?

offerings.description: Combines external asset discovery with checks informed by Mandiant’s frontline threat intelligence.
offerings.question: Can analysts tie a threat advisory to an affected asset and a responsible team?

offerings.description: Maps assets and exposures across both the organization and its third-party network.
offerings.question: Can we separate first-party remediation from supplier follow-up and track each independently?

threat-intelligence.title: Cyber threat intelligence
threat-intelligence.intro: If our CISO asks whether a campaign targeting our industry matters to us, one vendor can brief us on the actor, another can supply domain history for the investigation, and a platform can get both into the SOC. I’d start by asking who needs the answer and what they’ll do with it.
threat-intelligence.discoveryQuestion: Think about the last threat report someone forwarded you. What did you need to know, who made a decision, and what evidence was missing?

groups.question: Does the buyer need an analyst’s assessment, a recurring report, or a custom briefing?

offerings.description: Reports on adversary infrastructure, techniques and targets to help analysts prioritize threats and brief stakeholders.
offerings.question: Show a report that answers a question our CISO actually asked. What evidence supports its assessment?

offerings.description: Combines collection and analysis on threat actors and campaigns with reporting through its Unified Risk Platform.
offerings.question: How would you brief us on one campaign affecting our industry and geography?

offerings.description: Delivers tailored threat intelligence and analysis as an incident response service.
offerings.question: Can our incident commander submit a specific question? What turnaround and deliverable would we buy?

groups.need: Monitor cybercrime and dark web sources
groups.question: Can the provider corroborate a claim and show why it matters to this organization?

offerings.description: Combines primary-source collection and analyst reporting on cybercrime, identity, fraud and other security threats.
offerings.question: Which findings include the original context and an analyst’s assessment of credibility?

offerings.description: Provides actor-focused reporting sourced from criminal communities, including analyst research and customer-directed intelligence requirements.
offerings.question: Can the research team answer a question about a criminal group relevant to our business?

offerings.description: Brings underground discussions, actor identities, infrastructure and victim data together for investigations.
offerings.question: How do you distinguish a claim in a forum from independently corroborated activity?

offerings.description: Monitors attacker activity and supports investigations. Its Monitor integration can deliver clear, deep and dark web intelligence to Microsoft Sentinel.
offerings.question: When a monitored organization is mentioned, what source evidence reaches our analysts?

offerings.description: Collects signals from open and underground sources and relates credential exposure, ransomware activity and actor behavior to the organization.
offerings.question: Could an analyst link an alert to our company or a supplier and judge how reliable it is?

offerings.description: Offers threat research and monitoring across digital risks, including dark web and brand-related activity.
offerings.question: Which items identify our organization specifically, and which describe broader industry risk?

groups.question: What observation links a suspicious domain or host to a wider campaign?

offerings.description: Iris Investigate maps domain infrastructure. Iris Enrich adds domain context to indicators in security workflows.
offerings.question: What infrastructure relationships can an analyst substantiate, and when were they last observed?

offerings.offering: Silent Push platform and intelligence feeds
offerings.description: Uses DNS history, registration data, certificates and web observations to identify infrastructure associated with suspicious behavior.
offerings.question: What corroborating observations and confidence are attached to an infrastructure alert?

offerings.description: Adds threat-specific data to the Censys Platform for investigating and tracking adversary infrastructure.
offerings.question: What evidence supports an infrastructure link, and how does it change over time?

groups.question: Does new context change what the analyst does in an investigation?

offerings.description: Brings Mandiant research, VirusTotal community data and Google visibility into investigations and triage. Google offers different subscription tiers.
offerings.question: Which sources and API volumes come with the tier our analysts would use?

offerings.description: Packages adversary profiles, threat reporting and intelligence for Falcon security operations workflows.
offerings.question: What context does our SOC receive beyond the Falcon entitlements we already own?

offerings.question: Which intelligence can analysts access under our Defender and Sentinel licenses?

offerings.question: Which requests go to Unit 42 analysts, and what intelligence appears directly in Cortex?

groups.question: Are we buying new intelligence, the platform to manage it, or both?

offerings.description: An open-source threat intelligence platform that brings external and internal sources into a STIX-based knowledge graph for analysis and sharing.
offerings.question: Which sources must we bring or license, and how will we maintain their connectors?

offerings.description: Combines threat intelligence management and security operations workflows, including researching and organizing incoming intelligence.
offerings.question: What happens when two feeds disagree about an indicator or its confidence?

offerings.question: Can our existing feeds be prioritized and distributed to our tools with their source context intact?

offerings.question: Can analysts see which source supported an assessment and where it was delivered?

industry.evidence: Frost & Sullivan forecast 33.5% compound annual growth in global EASM revenue from 2024 to 2029.
industry.interpretation: Analyst forecast, December 2024. This figure is a growth rate. The public excerpt does not establish realized 2026 revenue.

industry.evidence: Grand View Research estimates the 2025 global threat intelligence market at $18.4B and forecasts $20.1B for 2026.
industry.interpretation: Analyst estimate and forecast. Its scope includes solutions and services, including SIEM-related applications. A specialist intelligence feed addresses a narrower market.

industry.evidence: Vulnerability exploitation was the initial access vector in 31% of the 2026 Verizon DBIR reporting dataset. The primary incident window was Nov 2024 to Oct 2025.
industry.interpretation: Observed breach data, figure 5 excludes Error and Misuse. This indicates urgency around exposed weaknesses. It does not measure EASM spend or prevention.

industry.evidence: Censys documents a workflow for discovering and attributing external assets across acquired and divested business units.
industry.interpretation: Vendor documentation. A GTM hypothesis is that a gap between legal ownership and the security inventory creates urgency.

industry.evidence: Microsoft bills on approved inventory using defined host/IP combinations, domains and IPs. IONIX describes annual pricing by discovered fully qualified domain names and service package.
industry.interpretation: Vendor terms. Model both quotes on one customer footprint and a plausible acquisition before comparing totals.

industry.evidence: Tenable’s acquisition of Bit Discovery added external discovery to its exposure tools. Securonix acquired ThreatQuotient, the company behind ThreatQ.
industry.interpretation: Company announcements. Ask what the current contract includes, who runs the module, and whether the required data is an add-on.

industry.evidence: Google lists annual subscriptions with an API-call allowance by tier and offers extra API packs. Cisco offers tailored Talos intelligence as a service.
industry.interpretation: Vendor packaging. Compare subscription coverage, API consumption, analyst access, and rights to share outputs with clients.

industry.evidence: FIRST describes a priority intelligence requirement as a way to direct work toward a stakeholder’s information need. NIST describes goals, sources and sharing rules for threat information.
industry.interpretation: Practitioner guidance. In discovery, write down a real stakeholder question, who consumes the answer and when it expires.

industry.evidence: STIX 2.1 gives threat data a structured representation. TAXII 2.1 specifies a protocol for moving that information between systems.
industry.interpretation: OASIS standards, June 2021. In evaluation, confirm that confidence, observation times and handling restrictions survive delivery.

situations.participants: Exposure lead, IT asset owner, integration lead
situations.question: What did the last acquisition add that your inventory still misses?
situations.measure: Count newly confirmed, in-scope assets absent from the prior inventory. Divide misattributions by reviewed discoveries.

situations.question: Walk me through the last internet-facing finding engineering disputed.
situations.measure: Measure time from discovery to owner acceptance and the share of remediated findings independently rechecked.

situations.question: Which external discoveries were unique to the module you already pay for?
situations.measure: Compare matched assets, owner-confirmed net-new assets and the annual cost under the same scope.

situations.question: What decision follows the briefing? Which sectors, geographies and threats would change that decision?
situations.measure: Review a briefing against a written priority intelligence requirement. Record whether the decision maker took an action.

situations.question: Which report changed a triage decision or led you to update a detection last month?
situations.measure: Measure time to a documented decision and the share of sampled reports that led to an investigation or detection review.

situations.question: When someone claims to have company data, how do you establish credibility and assign an owner?
situations.measure: Review a sample for organization relevance, provenance and duplicates. Track time to an owner’s decision.

situations.question: How do you handle the same indicator arriving from two providers with different dates and confidence?
situations.measure: Use sample records to verify deduplication, source retention, expiry and delivery into one downstream tool.

situations.participants: CTI analyst, exposure lead, remediation owner
situations.question: Do we know who is being targeted, which of our assets are affected, and who can confirm the fix?
situations.measure: Join a dated intelligence assessment to a confirmed owned asset. Track time to owner acceptance and to verified closure.

situations.question: Do we need to reconcile records from existing tools or discover internet-facing assets our tools missed?
situations.measure: CAASM emphasizes aggregation and reconciliation. Use owner-confirmed external discoveries to evaluate incremental EASM coverage.

situations.question: Is the gap an unknown public asset, cloud configuration context or testing depth on a known application?
situations.measure: Compare public discovery, cloud ownership context and depth of application testing separately.

situations.participants: Third-party risk, fraud or brand protection
situations.question: Are we remediating our own infrastructure, requesting a vendor fix, or handling brand impersonation?
situations.measure: Choose a first-party ticket, supplier escalation or brand-response workflow as the trial outcome.

situations.question: Who owns the exposure program from scoping through validation and remediation?
situations.measure: Continuous threat exposure management (CTEM) is a program. Scope which step each EASM or CTI purchase would support.

history.event: Palo Alto Networks completed the acquisition. Track Cortex Xpanse in the current directory.
Microsoft says it used RiskIQ infrastructure and data to build Defender EASM.
Tenable completed the acquisition and announced Tenable.asm. Its current product page uses Tenable One Attack Surface Management.
Bitsight completed the acquisition. Its CTI product is listed under Bitsight.
Mastercard completed the acquisition. Recorded Future remains the product brand used on both directories.
Searchlight states that Assetnote’s ASM platform is now Searchlight Exposure.
Securonix announced its acquisition of ThreatQuotient. The current platform is Securonix ThreatQ.
Dataminr describes its Cyber Defense suite, including Agentic TI Ops, as the first unified release following the acquisition.
Google completed its acquisition of Wiz. Wiz ASM and Mandiant ASM have distinct product pages.
Palo Alto Networks lists April 14, 2026 as the end-of-life date for Randori Recon.
Microsoft retired the standalone portal and the legacy Intel Explorer experience on August 1. Use the current Defender documentation for entitlement details.
